style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm of the ideal King -- titled 'of Solomon,' prayed by a father for his son or by the son for himself, and read by Israel and the church as the portrait of the Messiah's reign. It asks God to give the king His own justice, and then describes what that justice looks like when it lands: the poor judged rightly, the needy's children saved, the oppressor crushed; a people fearing God as long as the sun and moon endure, falling on the people like rain on mown grass; dominion from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth; kings of Tarshish and the islands, of Sheba and Seba, bringing tribute, all kings bowing, all nations serving -- because he rescues the needy who cry and have no helper, and their blood is precious in his sight. Grain on the mountaintops, cities flourishing like grass, a name that lasts as long as the sun, and all nations calling him blessed -- Abraham's promise fulfilled in David's son. The doxology at the end closes Book Two of the Psalter -- blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who alone does wonders; let the whole earth be filled with His glory, amen and amen -- and then the editor's note: the prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended. Isaac Watts turned it into 'Jesus Shall Reign.'

1.text: Of Solomon. O God, give the king Your judgments, and Your righteousness to the king's son.
1.amp: A Psalm for ['of', the KJV margin] Solomon [Shelomoh]. Give [natan] the king [melek] Your judgments [mishpat], O God [Elohim], and Your righteousness [tsedaqah] unto the king's son [ben].
1.notes: li-Shelomoh (H8010): 'of' or 'for' Solomon -- David's prayer for his heir, or Solomon's for himself. Elohim mishpatekha le-melekh ten (H430, H4941, H4428, H5414): give the king YOUR judgments -- justice as a gift from above, not a skill from below -- ve-tsidqatekha le-ben-melekh (H6666, H1121): Your righteousness to the king's son. The whole psalm is what happens when that prayer is answered.

2.text: May he judge Your people with righteousness and Your afflicted ones with justice.
2.amp: He shall judge [din] Your people [am] with righteousness [tsedek], and Your poor [ani -- afflicted] with judgment [mishpat -- justice].
2.notes: yadin ammekha be-tsedeq (H1777, H5971, H6664): he will judge YOUR people -- the people are God's, on loan to the king -- va-aniyyekha be-mishpat (H6041, H4941): and Your afflicted with justice. The first test of a reign is what the poor get from its courts.

3.text: May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills, through righteousness.
3.amp: The mountains [har] shall bring [nasa -- bear, carry] peace [shalom] to the people [am], and the little hills [givah], by righteousness [tsedaqah].
3.notes: yisu harim shalom la-am (H5375, H2022, H7965, H5971): the mountains CARRY shalom -- the terraced hillsides bearing peace like a crop -- u-gebaot bi-tsedaqah (H1389, H6666): and the hills, by righteousness. Under a just king even the geography is fruitful; the land's welfare tracks the throne's justice (cf. Isaiah 32:17).

4.text: May he do justice for the afflicted of the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
4.amp: He shall judge [shaphat] the poor [ani -- afflicted] of the people [am], he shall save [yasha] the children [ben] of the needy [evyon], and shall break in pieces [daka -- crush] the oppressor [ashaq].
4.notes: yishpot aniyye-am (H8199, H6041, H5971): justice for the afflicted -- yoshia li-bene evyon (H3467, H1121, H34): salvation for the needy's children -- vi-dakke osheq (H1792, H6231): and the oppressor CRUSHED, daka, Psalm 143:3's verb, now applied to the right target. The Messiah's justice has a violent edge, aimed at exploiters.

5.text: May they fear You as long as the sun and moon endure, through all generations.
5.amp: They shall fear [yare] You as long as [im -- with] the sun [shemesh] and moon [yareach] endure [panim -- before], throughout all generations [dor dorim].
5.notes: yiraukha im-shemesh ve-liphne yareach (H3372, H5973, H8121, H6440, H3394): they will fear You WITH the sun and BEFORE the moon -- as long as those two keep their appointments -- dor dorim (H1755): generation of generations. The reign's clock is astronomical; the Septuagint reads 'he shall endure', which is how the Greek and Latin church sang it.

6.text: May he descend like rain onto mown grass, like heavy showers that drench the earth.
6.amp: He shall come down [yarad] like rain [matar] upon the mown [gez -- shorn] grass: as showers [rebibim] that water [zarziph -- drench] the earth [eretz].
6.notes: yered ke-matar al-gez (H3381, H4306, H1488): the king descending like rain on a field just shorn -- the moment the grass is most vulnerable and most ready to grow -- ki-rebibim zarziph aretz (H7241, H2222, H776): like showers soaking the land. A reign that arrives as weather, not as an army.

7.text: In his days may the righteous one flourish, with abundance of peace until the moon exists no more.
7.amp: In his days [yom] shall the righteous [tsaddiq] flourish [parach -- blossom]; and abundance [rob] of peace [shalom] so long as the moon [yareach] endures ['till there be no moon', the KJV margin].
7.notes: yiphrach be-yamav tsaddiq (H6524, H3117, H6662): the righteous BLOSSOM in his days -- Psalm 92:12's palm -- ve-rob shalom ad-beli yareach (H7230, H7965, H3394): abundance of peace until there is no moon, the margin's literal. Peace with a lunar expiry date, which is to say none.

8.text: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River as far as the ends of the earth.
8.amp: He shall have dominion [radah] also from sea [yam] to sea, and from the river [nahar -- the Euphrates] unto the ends [ephes] of the earth [eretz].
8.notes: ve-yerd mi-yam ad-yam (H7287, H3220): dominion from sea to sea -- u-mi-nahar ad-aphse-aretz (H5104, H657, H776): from the River, the Euphrates, to the earth's ends. Zechariah 9:10 quotes the line for the King who comes riding a donkey; 'from sea to sea' became the motto on Canada's coat of arms.

9.text: Before him may the desert-dwellers bow before him, and may his enemies lick the dust.
9.amp: They that dwell in the wilderness [tsi -- desert-dwellers] shall bow [kara -- kneel] before [panim] him; and his enemies [oyeb] shall lick [lachak] the dust [afar].
9.notes: le-phanav yikhreu tsiyyim (H6440, H3766, H6728): the tsiyyim, the dwellers of the dry places -- the nomads at the empire's edge -- kneel -- ve-oyebav aphar yelachekhu (H341, H6083, H3897): and his enemies lick dust, the posture of Genesis 3:14's serpent and Micah 7:17's nations. Submission from the margins and from the enemies both.

10.text: May the kings of Tarshish and the coastlands render tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba present gifts.
10.amp: The kings [melek] of Tarshish [Tarshish] and of the isles [iy -- coastlands] shall bring [shub -- bring back] presents [minchah -- tribute]: the kings of Sheba [Sheba] and Seba [Seba] shall offer [qarab -- present] gifts [eshkar].
10.notes: malkhe Tarshish ve-iyyim minchah yashibu (H4428, H8659, H339, H4503, H7725): the far west -- Tarshish, probably Tartessos on Spain's coast, and the islands -- returning tribute; malkhe Sheba u-Seba eshkar yaqribu (H7614, H5434, H814, H7126): the far south -- Sheba in Arabia, Seba in Africa -- presenting gifts. The queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon was this verse's down payment; the Magi's gold, frankincense, and myrrh its fulfillment in the church's reading (cf. 1 Kings 10; Matthew 2:11).

11.text: May all kings fall down before him; may all nations serve him.
11.amp: Yea, all kings [melek] shall fall down [shachah -- bow] before him: all nations [goy] shall serve [abad] him.
11.notes: ve-yishtachavu-lo khol-melakhim (H7812, H4428): ALL kings prostrate -- kol-goyim yaabduhu (H1471, H5647): all nations serving him. The universal claim that no Davidic king ever cashed and that Philippians 2:10 says will be cashed.

12.text: For he will rescue the needy who cries for help, and the afflicted, and the one who has no helper.
12.amp: For he shall deliver [natsal] the needy [evyon] when he cries [shava -- cries for help]; the poor [ani -- afflicted] also, and him that has no helper [azar].
12.notes: ki-yatsil evyon meshavvea (H5337, H34, H7768): FOR -- the reason the kings bow -- he rescues the needy who is crying out -- ve-ani ve-en-ozer lo (H6041, H5826): and the afflicted, and the one with no helper at all. The empire of verses 8-11 rests on this: a king whose ear is tuned to the person nobody else will help.

13.text: He will have pity on the weak and the needy, and the souls of the needy he will save.
13.amp: He shall spare [chus -- pity, look with compassion on] the poor [dal -- weak, thin] and needy [evyon], and shall save [yasha] the souls [nephesh] of the needy.
13.notes: yachos al-dal ve-evyon (H2347, H1800, H34): chus is the eye's pity, the compassion that looks and cannot pass by -- ve-naphshot evyonim yoshia (H5315, H3467): and saves the needy's very lives. Evyon three times in two verses: the needy are this King's specialty.

14.text: From oppression and violence he will redeem their souls, and their blood will be precious in his eyes.
14.amp: He shall redeem [gaal -- act as kinsman-redeemer] their soul [nephesh] from deceit [tok -- oppression, fraud] and violence [chamas]: and precious [yaqar] shall their blood [dam] be in his sight [ayin].
14.notes: mi-tokh u-me-chamas yigal naphsham (H8496, H2555, H1350, H5315): gaal -- the kinsman-redeemer's verb, Boaz's verb -- the king as goel of the oppressed; ve-yeqar damam be-enav (H3365, H1818, H5869): and their blood PRECIOUS in his eyes -- the root of Psalm 116:15's 'precious' (there the adjective). A king who prices the poor man's blood high is the opposite of most kings Israel had known.

15.text: So may he live, and may the gold of Sheba be given to him; may prayer be made for him continually, and may he be blessed all day long.
15.amp: And he shall live [chayah], and to him shall be given ['one shall give', natan, the KJV margin] of the gold [zahab] of Sheba [Sheba]: prayer also shall be made [palal] for him continually [tamid]; and daily [yom] shall he be praised [barak -- blessed].
15.notes: vi-chi ve-yitten-lo mi-zehab Sheba (H2421, H5414, H2091, H7614): long live the king -- and Sheba's gold given him -- ve-yitpallel baado tamid (H6419, H8548): prayer FOR him continually -- kol-ha-yom yebarakhenhu (H3117, H1288): blessed all day. The people pray for the king who prays for them; 1 Timothy 2:2's prayer for kings stands in the stream this verse opens.

16.text: May there be an abundance of grain in the land, on the tops of the mountains; may its fruit wave like Lebanon, and may the people of the city flourish like the grass of the earth.
16.amp: There shall be an handful [pissah -- abundance, spread] of corn [bar -- grain] in the earth [eretz] upon the top [rosh] of the mountains [har]; the fruit [peri] thereof shall shake [raash -- rustle, wave] like Lebanon [Lebanon]: and they of the city [ir] shall flourish [tsuts -- blossom] like grass [eseb] of the earth.
16.notes: yehi phissat-bar ba-aretz be-rosh harim (H6451, H1250, H776, H7218, H2022): grain on the MOUNTAINTOPS -- the least arable ground -- pissah being read as 'handful' (KJV) or 'abundance' (WEB): even a handful there becomes a harvest; yirash ka-Lebanon piryo (H7493, H3844, H6529): its fruit rustling like the cedar forest -- ve-yatsitsu me-ir ke-eseb ha-aretz (H6692, H5892, H6212): city-dwellers sprouting like grass. Fertility as the signature of a righteous reign.

17.text: May his name endure forever; may his name continue as long as the sun -- and may men be blessed in him; may all nations call him blessed.
17.amp: His name [shem] shall endure ['be', the KJV margin] for ever [olam]: his name shall be continued [nun -- propagate, have posterity] as long as [panim -- before] the sun [shemesh]: and men shall be blessed [barak] in him: all nations [goy] shall call him blessed [ashar -- pronounce happy].
17.notes: yehi shemo le-olam (H8034, H5769): his name forever -- liphne-shemesh yinnon shemo (H6440, H8121, H5125): before the sun his name will have posterity, the margin's 'as a son to continue his father's name' -- ve-yitbarekhu bo kol-goyim yeashsheruhu (H1288, H1471, H833): all nations bless themselves in him and call him happy: Genesis 22:18 (and behind it 12:3), Abraham's promise, echoed almost word for word in the king's psalm. Galatians 3:16 names the Seed.

18.text: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things!
18.amp: Blessed [barak] be the LORD [YHWH] God [Elohim], the God of Israel [Yisrael], who only does [asah] wondrous things [pala].
18.notes: barukh YHWH Elohim Elohe Yisrael (H1288, H3068, H430, H3478): blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel -- the doxology that closes Book Two of the Psalter (Psalms 42-72) -- oseh niphlaot le-baddo (H6213, H6381): who does wonders ALONE. After a psalm of a king's glory, the last word insists whose the glory is.

19.text: Blessed be His glorious name forever and ever; let His glory fill the whole earth! Amen, and amen.
19.amp: And blessed [barak] be His glorious [kabod] name [shem] for ever [olam]: and let the whole earth [eretz] be filled [male] with His glory [kabod]; Amen [amen], and Amen.
19.notes: u-barukh shem kebodo le-olam (H1288, H8034, H3519, H5769): the Name of His glory blessed forever -- ve-yimmale khebodo et-kol-ha-aretz (H4390, H776): let His glory FILL the whole earth, the seraphim's line (cf. Isaiah 6:3) and Habakkuk 2:14's -- amen ve-amen (H543): the double seal.

20.text: Here the prayers of David son of Jesse come to their end.
20.amp: The prayers [tephillah] of David [David] the son [ben] of Jesse [Yishai] are ended [kalah -- completed].
20.notes: kallu tephillot David ben-Yishai (H3615, H8605, H1732, H1121, H3448): the prayers of David son of Jesse are finished -- an editor's colophon, not a verse of the poem -- the end of the second Davidic collection. Fittingly, the last 'prayer of David' is a prayer for his son, and through his son for the Son.
